description:
Montclair Public Library, Friends of the Howe House and Montclair Township present a community celebration of
freedom with food, fun, friends, family, and activities for all ages! Join us for games, face painting, balloon art,
performances, dancing and more. Bring your own chair and clack fan!

“Come Celebrate With Me” is a year-long series of programming honoring 100 years of observing Black history in America. Founded in 1926 by Carter G. Woodson, Negro History Week evolved into Black History Month, opening the door for additional annual commemorations such as Juneteenth, Black Music Month, Caribbean Heritage Month, Kwanzaa and more.

Montclair Public Library will honor the centennial of these commemorations in 2026 through a series of programs designed to engage and connect participants while highlighting and celebrating the experiences and contributions of people of African descent in the United States.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
The official meetup times are 8 AM and 9 AM respectively. If no one confirms for 8 AM but at least one person confirms for 9 AM then we start at 9 AM instead. If you are seriously attending any one event then please confirm one or the other start time in the comments so we can all coordinate and have an idea of what the actual attendance will be. You can confirm your arrival time on another person's confirmation (for 8 or 9) by liking that comment. Regardless of which official start time we use, you are welcome to show up any other time, although we are not responsible if we happen to disband early for any reason. The 12 PM cut-off time is only a general placeholder, not a guarantee, and we may all end sooner or later than that, depending on various factors. Plan accordingly and please use the comments for the benefit of our attendees as we try to please as many different time preferences as possible.

**ABOUT THE GROUP:** We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition. We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Chesapeake and Ohio 2 Day Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for two days point to point hiking on the Chesapeake and Ohio Canal and more!
Sunday we'll do between Brunswick and Monocacy Aqueduct, and Monday we'll head downstream from Monocacy Aqueduct.
After meeting Sunday at 9 at the aqueduct, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to the Holiday Inn.
We start right from the hotel, and follow the Valley Trail system downhill through a pleasant gully to downtown Brunswick.
Here, we'll cross the tracks and make our way onto the canal towpath to follow it to Monocacy Creek.
The first day will feature lovely riverside scenery, historic canal locks, and two major aqueducts. We'll take side trips to the river along the way.
We'll stay at the Holiday Inn, then the second day, we'll shuffle cars and hike between Monocacy Aqueduct and Sycamore Landing.
Both places have little lunch stops along them if needed, but everyone should come prepared with plenty of water and food just in case.
With the exception of under a mile through scenic downtown Brunswick, there is no road walking.
The first day has only 5 road access points, and the second has only 4, and not all of these are crossings.
This promises to be a beautiful, relaxing two days along the canal and Potomac River.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

About L’Alliance New York
Attracting over 150,000 visitors annually, L’Alliance New York is the city’s premier center for French language and francophone arts and cultures. As an independent, not-for-profit organization, L’Alliance New York’s mission is to enrich everyday lives with the spirit of joie de vivre through education, language, and culture. L’Alliance New York is proud to provide its members and students with engaging French language classes and audacious multi-disciplinary programming that celebrates the diversity of francophone cultures and creativity around the world. L’Alliance New York is internationally known for offering the largest selection of fully-immersive French language courses for students aged one to 101, and for its renowned cultural programming including the annual Bastille Day celebration that takes place on New York’s famed Madison Avenue, attracting over 50,000 visitors each year; the Crossing The Line arts and performance festival that engages NYC cultural institutions in bringing dynamic international artists to audiences; Animation First, the biggest animation festival in the U.S; and the Comic Arts Fest, celebrating the intersection of American and francophone comic arts.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: Jazz author talk - Henry Threadgill & Brent Hayes Edwards
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
A towering figure in modern jazz and creative music. Composer, saxophonist, flautist, bandleader. NEA Jazz Master, winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Music. THREADGILL will talk with memoir co-author EDWARDS (Columbia University) about his fascinating life in music, his service in Vietnam, his Chicago childhood, and beyond. Followed by a Q&A.






HENRY THREADGILL

Hailed by the New York Times as “perhaps the most important jazz composer of his generation,” Henry Threadgill has been celebrated for over forty years as one of the most original, forward-thinking composers and multi-instrumentalists in American music. His four-movement work, In for a Penny, In for a Pound, received the Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2016, one of only three jazz compositions to ever be so honored.






A Chicago native, Mr. Threadgill studied at the city’s American Conservatory of Music, majoring in composition, piano, and flute. A Vietnam veteran, he performed with the U.S. Army Concert Band. Mr. Threadgill is an early member of the Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians (AACM), dedicated to the performance of its members’ original music. Mr. Threadgill has also received a Guggenheim Fellowship, the Aaron Copland Award, and the Doris Duke Impact Award. Down Beat magazine’s International Jazz Critics Poll has five times distinguished him with its Best Composer Award. The Jazz Journalists Association honored him with its 2002 Composer of the Year Award and its Lifetime Achievement Award. Mr. Threadgill has released over thirty critically acclaimed albums.

​

Mr. Threadgill’s orchestral pieces, 1987’s Run Silent, Run Deep, Run Loud, Run and 1993’s Mix for Orchestra premiered at the Brooklyn Academy of Music. His many commissions include Mordine & Co. Dance Theater, Carnegie Hall, the New York Shakespeare Festival, Talujon Percussion Ensemble, Junge Philharmonic Salzburg Orchestra, the Biennale di Venezia, and the American Composers Orchestra. He has been composer in residence at University of California-Berkeley and the Atlantic Center of the Arts. Through the years, Mr. Threadgill has led, performed, and recorded with numerous groups, most recently Zooid and the Double Up Ensemble. In 2015, a two-day festival at New York’s Harlem Stage celebrated works spanning Mr. Threadgill’s career performed and reinterpreted by an all-star collection of musicians.





BRENT HAYES EDWARDS




B.A., Yale (1990); M.A., Columbia (1992); Ph.D., Columbia (1998). Brent Edwards writes and teaches on topics including African American literature, Francophone literature, theories of the African diaspora, translation studies, archive theory, black radical historiography, cultural politics in Paris in the 1920s and 1930s, surrealism, experimental poetics, and jazz.

His most recent book is is the author of Easily Slip into Another World: A Life in Music, the co-written autobiography of Pulitzer Prize-winning composer Henry Threadgill (Knopf, 2023), which was awarded a 2024 American Book Award and a 2024 Jazz Journalists Association Book of the Year Award for Biography or Autobiography. Edwards is also the author of Epistrophies: Jazz and the Literary Imagination (Harvard University Press, 2017), which won the 2018 ASCAP Foundation Virgil


Thomson Award for Outstanding Music Criticism as well as the 2019 Truman Capote Award for Literary Criticism; and The Practice of Diaspora: Literature, Translation, and the Rise of Black Internationalism (Harvard University Press, 2003), which was awarded the John Hope Franklin Prize of the American Studies Association, the Gilbert Chinard Prize of the Society for French Historical Studies, and runner-up for the James Russell Lowell Prize of the Modern Language Association. With Robert G. O’Meally and Farah Jasmine Griffin, he co-edited the collection Uptown Conversation: The New Jazz Studies (Columbia University Press, 2004).

Edwards has edited scholarly editions of Frederick Douglass’s My Bondage and My Freedom, Joseph Conrad’s Nostromo, W. E. B. Du Bois’s The Souls of Black Folk, and (in collaboration with Jean-Christophe Cloutier) Claude McKay’s Amiable with Big Teeth. With Eve Gianoncelli, Edwards edited Écrire le Monde Noir, a collection of the interwar writings of the pioneering


Martinican intellectual Paulette Nardal. Since 2014, he has served as the Harlem Renaissance period editor for the Norton Anthology of African American Literature.

From 2001-2011, Edwards was co-editor of the journal Social Text, and he is also a member of the editorial boards of Transition and Callaloo. Since 2021 he has served as the editor of PMLA, the flagship journal of the Modern Language Association. Edwards is also a translator, having published English-language versions of essays, poems, and fiction by authors including Edouard Glissant, Aimé Césaire, Jacques Derrida, Jean Baudrillard, Sony Labou Tansi, Paulette Nardal, and Monchoachi. His translation of Michel Leiris’s 1934 book Phantom Africa (Seagull Books, 2017), was completed with the support of a 2012 PEN/Heim Translation Fund Grant. Edwards was a 2015 Guggenheim Fellow, and in 2020 he was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

title: From OLTP to AI: Building a Modern Data Platform with Microsoft Fabric
description:
Cloud Data Driven
Operational databases such as MySQL and PostgreSQL power many applications, but turning this data into analytics can require complex pipelines. Microsoft Fabric provides a unified platform for data ingestion, transformation, and analytics.

In this talk, we will explore how to move data from operational databases into a Fabric Lakehouse and build a scalable analytics platform. We will cover ingestion patterns, medallion architecture, and practical lessons from building real data pipelines.

Attendees will learn how to design a simple and reliable architecture that connects transactional systems with modern analytics workflows.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Game Night: A Very Fey Drag Dungeons & Dragons
location: The Eclectic Chic Boutique, 547 Bloomfield Avenue, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Adventurers! Join us for a fun and fantastical one shot D&D campaign, facilitated by a magically whimsical Drag Dungeon Master. We embrace the quirky, the chaotic, and the downright silly. No experience necessary, we welcome players of all skill levels. We’re all about having a good laugh and creating unforgettable memories together. Players aged 16 and up are welcome to play. This is a safe space for all, including LGBTQIA+ and Neurodiverse folk. 
Players will be playing the one shot The Solstice Gala: Welcome, Dear Players, to the Seelie court’s Solstice Gala! Perhaps you’re a ranger or warlock who has harbored favor with an Archfey. Maybe you’re a native to the Fey wild looking to celebrate the Endless Sun. It’s possible, even, that you’re a mortal who has been whisked away and replaced by a changeling… who forgot they had a ticket to the Seelie Court’s largest party and now you’re filling their seat. Whatever the reason, you have earned your way into Titania’s banquet celebrating the Fey Solstice, when the Seelie Court welcomes continuous sun for the next century (in Fey time, of course). Chaos is sure to ensue– it’s the Feywild, after all. 
We will be playing a fully home brewed one shot in D&D 5e with an emphasis on roleplaying. Characters are welcome to be any level 5-8 and we will be using the point buy system to build our sheets. While it may be tempting to play a level 8 bard with max charisma for a social one shot, remember playing a low level fighter who can’t string elegance together to save their life might bring its own unique challenges and fun. We welcome you to the Feywild and hope you try the food and enjoy your stay!

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
The official meetup times are 8 AM and 9 AM respectively. If no one confirms for 8 AM but at least one person confirms for 9 AM then we start at 9 AM instead. If you are seriously attending any one event then please confirm one or the other start time in the comments so we can all coordinate and have an idea of what the actual attendance will be. You can confirm your arrival time on another person's confirmation (for 8 or 9) by liking that comment. Regardless of which official start time we use, you are welcome to show up any other time, although we are not responsible if we happen to disband early for any reason. The 12 PM cut-off time is only a general placeholder, not a guarantee, and we may all end sooner or later than that, depending on various factors. Plan accordingly and please use the comments for the benefit of our attendees as we try to please as many different time preferences as possible.

**ABOUT THE GROUP:** We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition. We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Hike with Dr. Kirk! 3-4 miles
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**Saturday June 27 9a-12pm**

Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation. Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the Rahway River up South Mountain. Focus on ecology and hydrology, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues.

**Good balance required. Children welcome. No dogs.**

Sponsored by South Mountain Conservancy and the Rahway River Watershed Association.

**Meet at Clipper Pavilion (Not by McLoone's) on Cherry Lane in West Orange.**

Advance registration required via [rahwayriver.org/calendar.html ](https://rahwayriver.org/calendar.html)

Email president@rahwayriver.org with questions.

title: 15 th Annual Taubman Paino Festival
location: Leshowitz Hall, Montclair State University, 1 Normal Avenue, Montclair, NJ, 07043, United States
description:
Montclair State University’s Cali School of Music presents the 15th Annual Taubman Piano Festival on June 27–28, 2026. The festival features two public piano recitals, with admission available at the door for $20. 
Saturday, June 27 at 4:00 p.m.
Esteban Castro 
Pianist and composer Esteban Castro has performed internationally at leading venues and festivals including the Montreux Jazz Festival, The Blue Note, Birdland, and NPR Tiny Desk. A full-scholarship student at The Juilliard School and a private student of Fred Hersch, Castro became the youngest-ever winner of the Montreux Jazz Piano Solo Competition at age 13. 
His recital will feature a variety of compositions and original improvisations. 
Sunday, June 28 at 4:00 p.m.
Fei-Fei 
Acclaimed for her poetic artistry and charismatic stage presence, pianist Fei-Fei is a winner of the Concert Artists Guild Competition and a top finalist at the 14th Van Cliburn International Piano Competition. She has performed worldwide as a soloist and recitalist, including appearances at Carnegie Hall and with major orchestras across the United States, Europe, Asia, and Central America. 
Her recital will include works by Beethoven, Rachmaninoff, and Chopin. 
For details, contact Dr. David Witten at wittend@montclair.edu.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
The official meetup times are 8 AM and 9 AM respectively. If no one confirms for 8 AM but at least one person confirms for 9 AM then we start at 9 AM instead. If you are seriously attending any one event then please confirm one or the other start time in the comments so we can all coordinate and have an idea of what the actual attendance will be. You can confirm your arrival time on another person's confirmation (for 8 or 9) by liking that comment. Regardless of which official start time we use, you are welcome to show up any other time, although we are not responsible if we happen to disband early for any reason. The 12 PM cut-off time is only a general placeholder, not a guarantee, and we may all end sooner or later than that, depending on various factors. Plan accordingly and please use the comments for the benefit of our attendees as we try to please as many different time preferences as possible.

**ABOUT THE GROUP:** We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition. We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: "We Hold These Truths": A 250th Celebration of the Declaration of Independence NEW
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
Note: This is a free Adult School class. Click below to register or on the Adult School Website.

What better way to commemorate the 250th Anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776 than by having local Montclair high school students read aloud the famous words that have inspired abolitionists, suffragists, civil rights leaders, labor organizers, and countless others to fight to extend liberty and equality more fully than at our nation’s founding? The program will also include a talk by Steve Golin, professor emeritus of Bloomfield College, on why its significance lies not only in what it achieved in 1776, but in how its words have continued to challenge every generation to live up to them. The program will also include free birthday cake for all! Kick start your July 4th plans by sharing in an uplifting and patriotic party!

Sponsored by the League of Women Voters of the Montclair Area

title: 15 th Annual Taubman Piano Festival
location: Leshowitz Hall, Montclair State University, 1 Normal Avenue, Montclair, NJ, 07043, United States
description:
Montclair State University’s Cali School of Music presents the 15th Annual Taubman Piano Festival on June 27–28, 2026. The festival features two public piano recitals, with admission available at the door for $20. 
Saturday, June 27 at 4:00 p.m.
Esteban Castro 
Pianist and composer Esteban Castro has performed internationally at leading venues and festivals including the Montreux Jazz Festival, The Blue Note, Birdland, and NPR Tiny Desk. A full-scholarship student at The Juilliard School and a private student of Fred Hersch, Castro became the youngest-ever winner of the Montreux Jazz Piano Solo Competition at age 13. 
His recital will feature a variety of compositions and original improvisations. 
Sunday, June 28 at 4:00 p.m.
Fei-Fei 
Acclaimed for her poetic artistry and charismatic stage presence, pianist Fei-Fei is a winner of the Concert Artists Guild Competition and a top finalist at the 14th Van Cliburn International Piano Competition. She has performed worldwide as a soloist and recitalist, including appearances at Carnegie Hall and with major orchestras across the United States, Europe, Asia, and Central America. 
Her recital will include works by Beethoven, Rachmaninoff, and Chopin. 
For details, contact Dr. David Witten at wittend@montclair.edu.

Discover the art of working on the potter’s wheel in this hands-on 6-week introductory course. Whether you're a complete beginner or looking to refine basic skills, this class offers a welcoming environment to explore the fundamentals of working with clay on the wheel.

You’ll learn the essential techniques of centering, pulling, shaping, and trimming clay to create functional forms like bowls and cups. As the course progresses, you’ll be introduced to glazing methods and the firing process, transforming your pieces into finished, food-safe ceramics. By the end of the session, you’ll have several unique, handmade pieces to take home and enjoy.

All clay, glaze, firings and tools are included.

For the first class, bring an apron or work clothes, sketchbook, writing implement and your curiosity!

description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
The official meetup times are 8 AM and 9 AM respectively. If no one confirms for 8 AM but at least one person confirms for 9 AM then we start at 9 AM instead. If you are seriously attending any one event then please confirm one or the other start time in the comments so we can all coordinate and have an idea of what the actual attendance will be. You can confirm your arrival time on another person's confirmation (for 8 or 9) by liking that comment. Regardless of which official start time we use, you are welcome to show up any other time, although we are not responsible if we happen to disband early for any reason. The 12 PM cut-off time is only a general placeholder, not a guarantee, and we may all end sooner or later than that, depending on various factors. Plan accordingly and please use the comments for the benefit of our attendees as we try to please as many different time preferences as possible.

**ABOUT THE GROUP:** We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition. We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Pepe Santana and Grupo Inkhay: Free Live Andean Concert NEW
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
Note: This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.


	
		
			
			This is the kickoff for the Paved with Promise suitcase exhibition, which will be installed in Montclair Public Library's lobby on July 1 by the Folklife Center of Northern New Jersey.
			
		
	


Enjoy the exciting live music of Pepe Santana, an Ecuadorian-born master musician based in New York City, with Grupo Inkhay, six musicians who play over two dozen musical instruments a variety of pan-pipes known as "sikus", "antaras" or "zampoñas". They also play end-nocthed vertical flutes called kenas, transverse flutes, whistles and ocarinas as well as an array of percussion instruments. 

Santana emigrated to the United States 38 years ago after the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965 commemorated in the Paved with Promise suitcase exhibition that will be installed in Montclair Public Library's lobby on July 1 by the Folklife Center of Northern New Jersey. The Andean pan-pipes Santana brought with him from Ecuador and lent to the Folklife Center are part of the display.

Santana has shared the musical traditions of the Andes, his lifelong passion, in venues such as the Lincoln Center, Alice Tully Hall, and Carnegie Hall, among many others. His emphasis on age-old sounds and rhythms has defined him as a true spokesman of traditional Andean music. 

Co-sponsored by the Folklife Center of Northern New Jersey

title: Mickalene Thomas: Subverting the Familiar Online NEW
description:
This is a free Adult School class. Click here to register on the Adult School website or register below.

Mickalene Thomas has given us vivid and multifaceted artworks—paintings, collage, photography, video, and site-specific installations. Her work addresses our common perceptions of beauty, sexuality, celebrity, and politics, and expands and subverts these notions in original and complex ways. The subject of a recent major international tour that began at The Broad in Los Angeles in May of 2024, traveled to The Barnes Foundation in Philadelphia on October 20, and culminated at The Hayward Gallery in London from February 11 to May 5, 2025, Mickalene Thomas has assumed her rightful place among the most important, original, and inspiring artists of the 21st century.

title: AI Governance for Cloud Data Platforms: From Policy to Practice
description:
Cloud Data Driven
As organizations deploy AI and analytics on modern cloud data platforms, governance often remains theoretical, documents exist, but execution breaks down in production. This session focuses on how to operationalize AI governance directly within cloud data platforms so that trust, compliance, and scalability are built into everyday workflows.

The session covers practical patterns for embedding governance into data pipelines and AI workflows, including data quality controls, lineage and metadata, access governance, model oversight, and audit-ready evidence. Attendees will learn why governance fails at scale, how to avoid common pitfalls, and how to align DataOps and MLOps practices to support reliable analytics and AI in the cloud.

This talk is framework-driven, vendor-neutral, and grounded in real-world challenges faced by teams running analytics and AI on cloud platforms.

title: Much Ado About Nothing - Opening Night SOLD OUT!
location: Van Vleck House & Gardens, 21 Van Vleck Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
The Montclair Foundation & Studio Players Announce an Immersive Production of Much Ado About Nothing Set for a July 2026 Debut 
Get ready for a Shakespearean takeover! The Montclair Foundation/Van Vleck House & Gardens and Studio Players are delighted to present William Shakespeare’s classic comedy of romance and intrigue, “Much Ado About Nothing,” opening July 10. This is no ordinary stage production; it’s an immersive theatrical experience. The grounds will be completely transformed into the site of a comedy of errors. Audience members will find themselves in the heart of the action as Shakespearean actors bring the story to life throughout the gardens 
Much Ado About Nothing 360° 
The play, originally set in and around a castle in 16th Century Messina, Italy, is structurally ideal for the Van Vleck location as it moves from lush interiors to cultivated exteriors, and the staging will create an immersive opportunity for attendees to explore the beauty of the Van Vleck estate while simultaneously enjoying one of the Bard’s most beloved comedies. Studio Players will begin casting the production in mid-March. 
Performances will be held on July 10th – 11th and July 16th- 18th from 7:00 PM – 8:00 PM, with rain dates to be announced. Join us for a VIP Opening Night celebration on Friday, July 10th at 6:00 PM, featuring a lively pre-show reception with champagne and hors d’oeuvres to kick off the production in style. Opening Night tickets are $75, while general admission tickets for all other performances are $50. Tickets are available at the link below or by contacting the box office at (973) 744-9752. 
 
  
About the Play 
Originally penned in 1598-1599, Much Ado About Nothing is a rollicking comedy centered around two romantic couples, the naive and wistful Claudio and Hero, and the more worldly-wise Benedick and Beatrice. Situated in and around a medieval castle in Messina, Sicily, the story unfolds as members of Don Pedro’s army descend on Leonato’s castle for a few weeks of rest and relaxation after claiming victory in battle. What follows is a witty examination of the nature of love involving trickery, mistaken identity, vengeful propositions, an exuberant masquerade ball, and a wedding gone horribly wrong. 
About Studio Players 
Studio Players (14 Alvin Place, Montclair, NJ) is the oldest continually-operating community theatre in Northern New Jersey–offering numerous opportunities for volunteers to participate at all levels (producing, directing, designing, performing, and technical support) in productions of exciting new plays and beloved classics. Founded in 1937 on the site of an old clock factory, our non-profit organization is now a staple of Montclair’s ever-growing arts scene, and we pride ourselves in presenting quality productions featuring groups of artists that reflect the diversity of Montclair and the surrounding communities. For more information, please visit StudioPlayers.org

title: Los Toritos de Pucará: Peruvuan Craft Painting Workshop (Children & Adults)
location: Montclair Main - Children's Floor, Montclair Main - Green Room
description:
The Consulate General of Peru in Paterson offers a Torito de Pucará painting workshop for both adults and children. Through this activity, participants learn about the cultural significance of the Torito de Pucará while enjoying a relaxed and creative painting experience. Participants will take home their own painted Torito at the end of the workshop. Registration recommended.

 

About the Toritos de Pucará

The Toritos de Pucará are an iconic Peruvian craft originating from the town of Pucará, in the Puno region. These ceramic figures, which depict bulls adorned with vibrant colors and intricate patterns, have roots that trace back to pre-Hispanic times, influenced by the Pucará culture, which flourished between 500 B.C. and 200 A.D. in Peru’s highland region. The significance of the Toritos de Pucará is deeply connected to protection, prosperity, and fertility. Traditionally, they are placed on the rooftops of homes as amulets to attract good luck, abundant harvests, and protection for the family and household. The bull, a strong and resilient animal, is seen as a guardian that wards off negative energies and draws in abundance. Over time, and following the arrival of the Spanish, the Toritos de Pucará were incorporated into Christian beliefs, where the figure of the bull came to symbolize sacrifice and spiritual strength. In this way, these figures became a cultural icon of the Andean region, representing a syncretism between ancient agricultural traditions and new religious influences.

title: Everything Book Club, "To the Lighthouse" by Virginia Woolf
location: Montclair Main - Teen Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
After we read "1984," you asked for more classics so here we are! 

In this masterpiece of modernist literature, the Ramsay family, along with a group of their friends and guests, gather at their summer home on the Scottish coast, anticipating a long-promised trip to the lighthouse across the bay. In part one, the action revolves around Mrs. Ramsay. In part two, the family returns without her. If you've always meant to read this book, now's your chance! If you've read it before, let's explore it again together.

"I read this book like I eat chocolate, always intending to indulge in just a little bit, then finding myself inexorably unwilling to stop."—The Guardian

Born in 1882, Virginia Woolf is recognized as a major 20th-century author, a great novelist and essayist and a key figure in literary history. With her sister, the painter Vanessa Bell, she was drawn into the company of writers and artists later known as the Bloomsbury Group. Woolf struggled with mental illness all of her life and in 1941, fearing another attack, she drowned herself.

title: Introduction to Wheel Throwing Pottery NEW
description:
Note: This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Discover the art of working on the potter’s wheel in this hands-on 6-week introductory course. Whether you're a complete beginner or looking to refine basic skills, this class offers a welcoming environment to explore the fundamentals of working with clay on the wheel.

You’ll learn the essential techniques of centering, pulling, shaping, and trimming clay to create functional forms like bowls and cups. As the course progresses, you’ll be introduced to glazing methods and the firing process, transforming your pieces into finished, food-safe ceramics. By the end of the session, you’ll have several unique, handmade pieces to take home and enjoy.

All clay, glaze, firings and tools are included.

For the first class, bring an apron or work clothes, sketchbook, writing implement and your curiosity!

title: Create Your Own Indian Paper Quill Earrings NEW
location: Montclair Main - Classroom, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Paper quilling arrived in India as a modernized handicraft in the late 20th centuries. Indian artisans quickly embraced the medium, pairing the technique with the country's rich history of paper-making and making it their own. In this class traditional artist and artisan Ajita Shah teaches you how to create a variety of beautiful and unusual earrings out of paper quills.

Co-sponsored by the Folklife Center of Northern New Jersey. This program goes along with the Paved With Promise suitcase exhibition commemorating the 1965 Immigration and Nationality Act which opened up the United States to groups in Asia, South America and other areas that had been previously restricted.

title: Women and Money Roundtable - How to Make Sense of Today's Financial Markets
description:
A virtual, lively, and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio. 


Julia Strayer and Liz Maccarone will lead a lively and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio.

This is a virtual program that takes place over Zoom. As the date approaches, you will receive an email with the Zoom link.

About the Presenters

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Previously, Julia worked in marketing for 9 years with Merrill. Julia has a BA from Ohio State University and an MBA from New York University’s Stern School of Business. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. title: Summer at Van Vleck - Nature Journaling
location: Van Vleck House & Gardens, 21 Van Vleck Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
Summer at Van Vleck 
Partner Program with the Montclair Institute for Lifelong Learning 
Thursdays, July 16 – Aug 20, 1:30 PM – 2:30 PM 
July 16 – Nature Journaling – Slow down and notice the textures of the natural world in this creative nature journaling class.  Using leaves, bark, stones, and other found objects in the Gardens, we’ll experiment with texture rubbings and transfer their patterns onto the pages of our journals while experimenting with color, layering and the pressures our marks make.  As we play, you will have the opportunity to explore a simple writing prompt inspired by the process.  Part art-making, part free-thought writing, this class invites curiosity, creativity and a connection with nature.  No art or writing experience necessary to join along. 
July 23 – Seasonal Interest Summer Tour – Join Laura Roberts, Director of Horticulture at The Montclair Foundation – Van Vleck House & Gardens, for a journey through the beauty of the season. Tour highlights will include many beautiful blooming specimens as well as a visit to our Kitchen Garden which showcases a bountiful collection of veggies, greens, and herbs. Outdoor tour, so please dress for the weather with appropriate footwear. 
July 30 – Collage Art – Unplug and make something unexpectedly beautiful.  In this hands-on collage class, we’ll be using natural materials from the Gardens, and turn them into your personal masterpiece. Learn about composition, texture, color and layering, while using leaves, petals, moss, bark seed and other found objects.  No art experience needed – just curiosity and desire to play and turn found objects into a one-of-a-kind piece of art to treasure. 
Aug 6 – Qigong – Through careful balancing forms and gentle breath awareness, you’ll connect to your body’s wisdom in the natural beauty of the Van Vleck garden. 
No experience necessary; bring a yoga mat or towel and an open mind. Instructor: Jodi Brooks. 
Aug 13 – Drought Resistant Plants – Join us for a walking tour of the drought resistant plants thriving in the gardens of Van Vleck and learn why they are so tolerant of our New Jersey summers. Instructor: Laura Roberts, Director of Horticulture 
Aug 20 – Guided Nature Walk  – Spend an afternoon in the gardens of Van Vleck with Volunteer Naturalist Jenny Aley. Search for birds and other animals, as well as the signs they leave behind. Learn interesting facts and information about the wildlife we share our backyards with.  
This class is a Partner Program with the Montclair Institute for Lifelong Learning. To register please visit: http://schedulesplus.com/montclair/kiosk

title: Much Ado About Nothing - immersive production SOLD OUT!
location: Van Vleck House & Gardens, 21 Van Vleck Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
The Montclair Foundation & Studio Players Announce an Immersive Production of Much Ado About Nothing Set for a July 2026 Debut 
Get ready for a Shakespearean takeover! The Montclair Foundation/Van Vleck House & Gardens and Studio Players are delighted to present William Shakespeare’s classic comedy of romance and intrigue, “Much Ado About Nothing,” opening July 10. This is no ordinary stage production; it’s an immersive theatrical experience. The grounds will be completely transformed into the site of a comedy of errors. Audience members will find themselves in the heart of the action as Shakespearean actors bring the story to life throughout the gardens 
Much Ado About Nothing 360° 
The play, originally set in and around a castle in 16th Century Messina, Italy, is structurally ideal for the Van Vleck location as it moves from lush interiors to cultivated exteriors, and the staging will create an immersive opportunity for attendees to explore the beauty of the Van Vleck estate while simultaneously enjoying one of the Bard’s most beloved comedies. Studio Players will begin casting the production in mid-March. 
Performances will be held on July 10th – 11th and July 16th- 18th from 7:00 PM – 8:00 PM, with rain dates to be announced. Join us for a VIP Opening Night celebration on Friday, July 10th at 6:00 PM, featuring a lively pre-show reception with champagne and hors d’oeuvres to kick off the production in style. Opening Night tickets are $75, while general admission tickets for all other performances are $50. Tickets are available at the link below or by contacting the box office at (973) 744-9752. 
 
  
About the Play 
Originally penned in 1598-1599, Much Ado About Nothing is a rollicking comedy centered around two romantic couples, the naive and wistful Claudio and Hero, and the more worldly-wise Benedick and Beatrice. Situated in and around a medieval castle in Messina, Sicily, the story unfolds as members of Don Pedro’s army descend on Leonato’s castle for a few weeks of rest and relaxation after claiming victory in battle. What follows is a witty examination of the nature of love involving trickery, mistaken identity, vengeful propositions, an exuberant masquerade ball, and a wedding gone horribly wrong. 
About Studio Players 
Studio Players (14 Alvin Place, Montclair, NJ) is the oldest continually-operating community theatre in Northern New Jersey–offering numerous opportunities for volunteers to participate at all levels (producing, directing, designing, performing, and technical support) in productions of exciting new plays and beloved classics. Founded in 1937 on the site of an old clock factory, our non-profit organization is now a staple of Montclair’s ever-growing arts scene, and we pride ourselves in presenting quality productions featuring groups of artists that reflect the diversity of Montclair and the surrounding communities. For more information, please visit StudioPlayers.org

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

Class may be cancelled due to weather if no indoor space is available.

Individual Class: $15 Members / $20 General Public 
Pre Registration is required.  There are no drop-ins for this class.

title: Help Desk - Bring Your Laptop, Yourself, and Your WordPress Problems
description:
WordPress Montclair Meetup
If you are running a WordPress site and are having issues and would like some help, then this Meetup is for you!

If you know some things, expert or not, and want to give back to the WordPress community, then this Meetup is for you too!

We will do our best to match a problem with a problem-solver. On-site and in real-time. Just bring yourself, your laptop, and your WordPress problems.

It's OK if you attend and only want to observe. We recognize this is how people learn. Given our time limit of two hours, we may not be able to solve everyone's issues, but we will try! If you are seeking help, please come prepared. Have your web site loaded in a browser, have your WordPress admin ready, along with a short list of issues you are trying to solve.

People helping are volunteers and may not be experts. There is risk to breaking your site! Please do not bring client or business sites that can impact reputations or revenue. If you have a staging site we can test things with, that is always preferred. If it is a production site, please create a site backup before having someone do any work on your site.

If you cannot find the group, please ask the front desk where the WordPress meetup group is meeting.

**PARKING**:
We've been asked to not park in the United Way lot behind the library as it could result in a parking ticket. Please find street parking or a parking deck.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - July meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - August meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.
source: Meetup: Board Game Night at Verona Inn

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Council On Ministries- Multi Platform
description: The UUCM Council on Ministries (CoM) exists to report to UUCM, its Board and Co-Ministers on how our programs are accomplishing their particular mission while also furthering the broader mission of UUCM. Special attention is paid to any systemic or cultural obstacles hindering our ability to fulfill our mission as well as any conflicts. Its primary goals are to maintain UUCM's Mission & Vision, restore trust and relationship when frayed, and to keep all our interactions in line with UUCM's covenant. Best practices, connectivity, cross-pollination and successes are also reported. The CoM also provides assistance evaluating our ministries periodically at the discretion of the Board. Please welcome Council on Ministries liaisons into your meetings and planning when they request to observe your functioning; share with them also your minutes and other documents when requested. title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

description:
Join NEEC for a festive evening celebrating another year
of community, sustainability, and bountiful harvests.
  
Dine on a delicious Mexican buffet, catered by Mezoco. Enjoy live music. Bid on wonderful silent auction items. 
All proceeds go toward NEEC projects — our six community gardens, 18 Free Little Pantries, and three pollinator gardens. With your help, we can continue to feed the food insecure and advocate for a more sustainable community. 
For tickets, visit NEECfiesta2026.eventbrite.com. 
We are excited to invite community organizations, businesses, and individuals to become sponsors. For more information about sponsorship opportunities, email Amanda at amccabe@neearth.org.
